Experiment.summary: Br promotes plant growth by binding to cell surface receptors and activating intracellular signaling proteins.

c1.text: Steroid hormones generally have low polarity and easily penetrate the cell membrane, whereas peptide hormones have high polarity and cannot penetrate.

c2.text: Peptide hormones bind to receptors on the cell surface and activate intracellular signaling proteins through receptor structural changes.

c3.text: Animal steroid hormones penetrate the cell membrane easily.

c4.text: The plant steroid hormone brassinolide (Br) promotes plant growth but cannot penetrate the cell membrane easily.

c5.text: Br promotes plant growth by binding to cell surface receptors and activating intracellular signaling proteins.

c6.text: Among Arabidopsis mutants, mutant A and mutant B were isolated, one having a defect only in the Br biosynthesis gene and the other only in the Br receptor gene.

c7.text: Both mutant A and mutant B showed a growth-inhibited phenotype compared to the wild type.

c8.text: When Br was applied, the inhibited growth of A was not restored, but B’s growth was restored.

c9.text: Mutant C showed a growth-inhibited phenotype due solely to a mutation in the gene for the signaling protein that recognizes structural changes in the Br receptor.

c10.text: If a growth-inhibited mutant's growth is restored by Br application, it has a defect in Br biosynthesis; if not restored, it has a defect in the Br receptor.

c11.text: A cannot synthesize Br, and B has a defect in the Br receptor.

c12.text: B cannot synthesize Br, and A has a defect in the Br receptor.

c13.text: Since mutant C has a defect in the intracellular signaling protein, applying Br cannot restore C's inhibited growth.

c14.text: After Br treatment, B's growth is restored while C's growth remains inhibited, so B and C show different phenotypes.

c15.text: After Br treatment, B and C show similar phenotypes.

h1.text: The difference in membrane permeability between animal and plant steroid hormones is determined only by polarity.

h2.text: Br is more polar than animal steroid hormones.

a.note: If permeability depends only on polarity, then because animal steroids cross easily (c3) while Br does not (c4), Br must be more polar (h2).

b.note: Experiment infers c12 (B is biosynthesis mutant, A is receptor mutant) from rescue results (c8, c10), so it cannot build an argument for c11.

c.note: Experiment derives that B recovers while C does not recover (c14), which is contrary to c15; thus c15 does not hold.
